symbol_definitions: x_i: observation i; n: sample size; x-bar: sample mean; s: sample standard deviation.
mathematical_explanation: The mean is the arithmetic center; the sample SD describes spread around that mean.
scope_note: The SD uses n−1 for a sample; mean and SD can be misleading for highly skewed distributions.

symbol_definitions: Q_p: sample quantile at probability p.
mathematical_explanation: The median is the halfway quantile; the IQR covers the middle half of observations.
scope_note: Exact sample quantiles depend on the chosen interpolation convention.

symbol_definitions: n_k: count in category k; n: total nonmissing cases; 1(·): indicator function.
mathematical_explanation: Counts summarize category prevalence; proportions express counts relative to the chosen denominator.
scope_note: Report missing values and weighted denominators explicitly where relevant.

symbol_definitions: x_i, y_i: paired observations; x-bar, y-bar: sample means.
mathematical_explanation: Pearson r quantifies the direction and strength of a linear association.
scope_note: Correlation does not establish causation; nonlinear patterns and influential points may mislead.

symbol_definitions: R_x, R_y: ranks of the observed x and y values (average ranks for ties).
mathematical_explanation: Spearman correlation applies Pearson correlation to ranked variables, capturing monotonic relationships.
scope_note: The shortcut 1−6Σd²/[n(n²−1)] is exact only without ties.

symbol_definitions: x-bar_g: group mean; s_g²: group sample variance; n_g: group size; s_p²: pooled variance.
mathematical_explanation: Tests the difference between two independent population means under a pooled-variance model.
scope_note: The pooled-variance test assumes equal population variances; otherwise consider Welch’s test.

symbol_definitions: x-bar_g: group mean; s_g²: sample variance; n_g: group size.
mathematical_explanation: Tests the difference between two independent means without requiring equal population variances.
scope_note: Uses Welch–Satterthwaite approximate degrees of freedom; independence still matters.

symbol_definitions: d_i: within-pair difference; d-bar: mean difference; s_d: SD of differences; n: paired observations.
mathematical_explanation: Tests whether the mean within-person or matched-pair change equals zero.
scope_note: Inference concerns the distribution of differences, not normality of each raw measurement.

symbol_definitions: R_1: sum of ranks in group 1 after pooling; n_1: group 1 size.
mathematical_explanation: The Mann–Whitney statistic measures relative ordering of two independent groups.
scope_note: Not generally a test of medians alone; interpreting it as a location shift requires similar distribution shapes.

symbol_definitions: d_i: nonzero paired difference; rank(|d_i|): rank of its absolute magnitude.
mathematical_explanation: Tests signed differences using both sign and relative magnitude.
scope_note: The familiar location interpretation requires a suitably symmetric difference distribution; zeros and ties need handling.

symbol_definitions: MS_between: between-group mean square; MS_within: pooled within-group mean square.
mathematical_explanation: Tests whether all group population means can be treated as equal in a one-factor model.
scope_note: Standard one-way ANOVA assumes independent errors and homogeneous variances; F itself does not identify which groups differ.

symbol_definitions: i,j: levels of two categorical factors; k: observation; α,β: main effects; (αβ): interaction.
mathematical_explanation: Separates differences attributable to two factors and their interaction.
scope_note: Interpret main effects carefully when the interaction is present; balanced designs simplify interpretation.

symbol_definitions: i: participant; t: repeated-measure level; τ_t: within-person factor effect; b_i: subject effect.
mathematical_explanation: Represents repeated observations on the same individual and compares within-person means.
scope_note: This is a schematic representation; classical repeated-measures ANOVA also imposes covariance requirements (including sphericity for >2 levels).

symbol_definitions: g: independent group; t: repeated timepoint; i: subject nested in group; α: group effect; τ: time effect; (ατ): interaction; b: subject effect.
mathematical_explanation: The group-by-time interaction tests whether groups change differently across repeated measurements.
scope_note: The model alone does not prove causality; assignment and causal design assumptions are separate. Classical ANOVA requires appropriate covariance assumptions.

symbol_definitions: Y: continuous outcome; G: group indicator; X: covariate; τ: adjusted group contrast.
mathematical_explanation: ANCOVA compares groups while adjusting for a preselected continuous covariate.
scope_note: A shared covariate slope is assumed in this version; adjusting for post-treatment variables may bias causal estimates.

symbol_definitions: k: groups; N: total size; n_j: group size; R-bar_j: mean pooled rank in group j.
mathematical_explanation: Compares distributions across independent groups using ranks.
scope_note: Shown without tie correction; it is not inherently a test of medians unless shapes are comparable.

symbol_definitions: n: complete blocks or participants; k: within-block conditions; R_.j: sum of within-block ranks for condition j.
mathematical_explanation: Compares repeated conditions by ranking measurements within each participant or block.
scope_note: Requires matched complete blocks in its classical form; ties require a correction.

symbol_definitions: O_ij: observed cell count; E_ij: expected cell count under independence; n: total count.
mathematical_explanation: Compares the observed table to expected counts assuming the categorical variables are independent.
scope_note: Sparse expected counts compromise the chi-square approximation; consider an exact procedure when appropriate.

symbol_definitions: a: upper-left cell count in a 2×2 table; r1,r2: row totals; c1: first-column total; n: grand total.
mathematical_explanation: Provides the conditional probability of each possible 2×2 table given fixed margins.
scope_note: Two-sided p-values require a stated convention; inference relies on the data-generating and sampling design.

symbol_definitions: β0: intercept; β1: expected outcome change per one-unit x increase; ε: error.
mathematical_explanation: Models the conditional mean outcome as a linear function of one predictor.
scope_note: A linear association alone is not causal; error assumptions matter for inference.

symbol_definitions: p: number of predictors; β_j: partial regression coefficients; ε: error.
mathematical_explanation: Models the mean outcome using several predictors simultaneously.
scope_note: Coefficient interpretations are conditional on other included predictors; collinearity can increase uncertainty.

symbol_definitions: p_i=P(Y_i=1|x_i); β: log-odds coefficients; exp(β): conditional odds ratios.
mathematical_explanation: Links binary outcome probability to predictors through the log-odds.
scope_note: Odds ratios differ from risk ratios; fitted probabilities need not demonstrate calibration or causality.

symbol_definitions: μ_i: expected count; x_i: covariate vector; β: log-rate or log-count coefficients depending on offsets.
mathematical_explanation: Models expected event counts or rates using a log link.
scope_note: Poisson variance equals its mean; overdispersion and exposure offsets require evaluation.

symbol_definitions: Xβ: fixed effects; Zb: group or subject-specific random effects; ε: residual errors.
mathematical_explanation: Models continuous outcomes with correlations induced by repeated or clustered measurements.
scope_note: Random-effect distribution and residual covariance assumptions affect inference; random effects are not always identifiable.

symbol_definitions: g: link function; β: fixed coefficients; b: random effects; Y: possibly non-Gaussian outcome.
mathematical_explanation: Extends regression for non-Gaussian outcomes to repeated and clustered measurements.
scope_note: Interpretation is usually conditional on random effects; suitable distributions and link functions depend on outcome type.

symbol_definitions: S: sample covariance or correlation matrix; w: principal-component loading direction.
mathematical_explanation: The first principal component is the direction of maximum sample variance; later components are orthogonal.
scope_note: Components describe variance, not necessarily meaningful latent causes; scale choices strongly affect results.

symbol_definitions: Λ: factor loadings; f: latent factors; Φ: factor covariance; Ψ: unique variance matrix.
mathematical_explanation: Represents observed covariation through a smaller set of common latent factors.
scope_note: Factor number and rotation affect interpretation; an exploratory factor solution is not causal proof.

symbol_definitions: G(t): Gini impurity at node t; p_k|t: proportion of class k at node t.
mathematical_explanation: A classification tree chooses splits that reduce a criterion such as impurity.
scope_note: This is one common classification-tree criterion; regression trees often minimize squared error instead.

symbol_definitions: B: number of trees; f-b(x): prediction from tree b.
mathematical_explanation: Regression random forests average predictions from trees grown on resampled data with feature randomness.
scope_note: Classification forests aggregate class votes or probabilities; this equation is for regression output.

symbol_definitions: T,C: treated and comparison groups; pre,post: periods; Y-bar: corresponding mean outcome.
mathematical_explanation: Subtracts the comparison group’s time change from the treated group’s time change.
scope_note: Causal interpretation requires a credible parallel-trends counterfactual and no major confounding shocks.

symbol_definitions: n_jk: joint count in category pair (j,k); 1(·): indicator.
mathematical_explanation: Cross-tabulation counts observations across combinations of two categorical variables.
scope_note: Cell percentages can be row-, column-, or table-based; report the denominator.

symbol_definitions: theta-hat: estimate; z: standard-normal critical value; SE: estimated standard error; 1−α: nominal coverage.
mathematical_explanation: A common large-sample Wald interval expresses sampling uncertainty around a parameter estimate.
scope_note: Not a universal CI formula; small samples, proportions, skewed estimators, and complex designs often need other intervals.

symbol_definitions: C,D: concordant/discordant observation pairs; T_x,T_y: pairs tied only on one variable.
mathematical_explanation: Kendall’s tau-b measures ordinal association based on concordance versus discordance, adjusting for ties.
scope_note: Exact definition of ties matters; the statistic is not a causal effect.

symbol_definitions: X_0/1: binary group indicator coded 0 or 1; Y: continuous measurement.
mathematical_explanation: Point-biserial correlation is Pearson correlation when one variable is binary.
scope_note: Coding reverses the sign; a binary predictor does not make the observed association causal.

symbol_definitions: r_ab: Pearson correlation between a and b; z: a single adjustment variable.
mathematical_explanation: Measures residual linear association between x and y after adjusting for z.
scope_note: This expression covers one adjustment variable; partial correlation does not remove unmeasured confounding.

symbol_definitions: x-bar: sample mean; μ0: hypothesized population mean; s: sample SD; n: sample size.
mathematical_explanation: Tests a sample mean against a prespecified reference value.
scope_note: Independence and sampling distribution assumptions determine validity of the t approximation.

symbol_definitions: w_j: inverse-variance weight; n_j: group size; s_j²: group variance; x-bar_j: group mean.
mathematical_explanation: Welch ANOVA compares group means using precision-weighted group estimates.
scope_note: These are weights and the pooled weighted mean, not the complete Welch F test; its test statistic uses an additional degrees-of-freedom correction.

symbol_definitions: E: within/error sum-of-products matrix; H: hypothesis sum-of-products matrix; |·|: determinant.
mathematical_explanation: Wilks’ lambda assesses multivariate mean separation across multiple continuous outcomes.
scope_note: One of several MANOVA statistics; sample size, covariance assumptions and multivariate outliers matter.

symbol_definitions: b,c: discordant off-diagonal cell counts in a paired 2×2 table.
mathematical_explanation: Tests whether paired binary responses change symmetrically across categories.
scope_note: This is the asymptotic uncorrected form; sparse discordant pairs favor an exact version.

symbol_definitions: p: polynomial degree; β_j: coefficients; x: predictor.
mathematical_explanation: Allows a curved conditional mean while remaining linear in model coefficients.
scope_note: High-degree polynomials may overfit or extrapolate poorly.

symbol_definitions: g: link function; f_j: smooth function of predictor j; β0: intercept.
mathematical_explanation: GAMs add flexible smooth relationships rather than imposing a strictly linear predictor effect.
scope_note: Smoothing flexibility and inference depend on basis and penalty choices; additive terms omit interactions unless specified.

symbol_definitions: K: reference outcome category; k: another category; α_k,β_k: category-specific coefficients.
mathematical_explanation: Models nominal outcomes by comparing each category’s log-odds to a reference category.
scope_note: This baseline-category specification is for unordered outcomes; estimates depend on the reference group.

symbol_definitions: k: ordered threshold; θ_k: threshold intercept; β: common coefficient vector.
mathematical_explanation: Models cumulative probabilities of an ordered outcome with common slopes across thresholds.
scope_note: The proportional-odds assumption can fail; slope signs follow the shown convention.

symbol_definitions: μ_i: mean count; α>0: overdispersion parameter (NB2 formulation).
mathematical_explanation: Negative-binomial regression allows count variance to exceed the mean.
scope_note: The displayed variance is NB2, one of several parameterizations; offsets may be needed for varying exposure.

symbol_definitions: π: structural-zero probability; μ: mean of the Poisson count component; k: positive count.
mathematical_explanation: A zero-inflated Poisson model combines a structural-zero process with an ordinary count process.
scope_note: This is one type of zero-inflated regression; zero-inflated negative binomial uses a different count component.

symbol_definitions: 0<Y_i<1; μ_i: conditional mean; φ>0: precision.
mathematical_explanation: Models a continuous proportion or rate strictly between zero and one.
scope_note: Exact zero and one observations require a modified model or separate treatment.

symbol_definitions: τ: chosen quantile (0<τ<1); ρ_τ: asymmetric check loss; β_τ: quantile coefficients.
mathematical_explanation: Estimates conditional outcome quantiles rather than the conditional mean.
scope_note: Different quantiles may have different covariate effects; standard OLS inference does not apply unchanged.

symbol_definitions: i: cluster; μ_i: marginal mean vector; D_i: derivative of μ_i with respect to β; V_i: working covariance.
mathematical_explanation: GEE estimates population-average regression effects while accounting for within-cluster correlation.
scope_note: A robust sandwich SE and sufficient independent clusters are important; the working correlation may be misspecified.

symbol_definitions: h: hazard rate; h0: baseline hazard; exp(β): hazard ratios for covariate changes.
mathematical_explanation: Models relative instantaneous event hazards without specifying the baseline hazard form.
scope_note: Proportional hazards and noninformative censoring assumptions need evaluation.

symbol_definitions: t_j: distinct event times; d_j: number of events at t_j; n_j: at-risk count just before t_j.
mathematical_explanation: The Kaplan–Meier estimator multiplies conditional survival probabilities across event times.
scope_note: Independent/noninformative censoring is important; estimates become unstable with few at risk.

symbol_definitions: O_j,E_j: observed and expected group events at event time j; V_j: corresponding variance contribution.
mathematical_explanation: The two-group log-rank test compares observed versus expected events across follow-up.
scope_note: Shown as a schematic two-group statistic; crossing hazards can reduce test power and complicate interpretation.

symbol_definitions: Λ: hypothesized factor-loading matrix; Φ: latent covariance; Θ: measurement-error covariance.
mathematical_explanation: Tests a prespecified factor-loading structure against observed covariance patterns.
scope_note: Identification and model fit must be checked; high fit does not establish construct validity alone.

symbol_definitions: X: explanatory variable; M: intermediate variable; Y: dependent variable; a,b,c: path coefficients.
mathematical_explanation: A path model represents several directed regression relations in one system.
scope_note: Specified arrows express causal hypotheses but fitted path coefficients alone do not prove causation.

symbol_definitions: η: endogenous latent variables; ξ: exogenous latent variables; B,Γ: structural paths; Λ_y: measurement loadings.
mathematical_explanation: SEM connects latent measurement models to a system of regression-like structural paths.
scope_note: This is one standard linear SEM formulation; identification, model assumptions and competing models remain essential.

symbol_definitions: X: exposure; M: mediator; Y: outcome; a,b: path coefficients; c-prime: direct-effect coefficient.
mathematical_explanation: In a simple linear mediation model the product ab represents the modeled indirect pathway.
scope_note: A causal indirect effect requires strong sequential ignorability and timing assumptions; effects need not decompose so simply for nonlinear models.

symbol_definitions: η0i: person-specific latent intercept; η1i: latent growth slope; t: time; ε: measurement residual.
mathematical_explanation: Models individual baseline levels and trajectories using latent growth factors.
scope_note: This is the linear-growth case; irregular time, nonlinear growth and missingness need appropriate specification.

symbol_definitions: B: lag operator; d: differencing order; φ and θ: autoregressive and moving-average lag polynomials.
mathematical_explanation: ARIMA describes dependence in a time series after differencing where needed.
scope_note: Stationarity and invertibility conditions apply to the modeled stationary component; seasonal variants extend this equation.

symbol_definitions: ℓ_t: smoothed level; α between 0 and 1: smoothing parameter; y_t: observed value.
mathematical_explanation: Simple exponential smoothing repeatedly updates the estimated level using recent errors.
scope_note: This is ETS(A,N,N) / simple exponential smoothing only; ETS also supports trend, seasonality and different error forms.

symbol_definitions: T: intervention time; β2: level shift; β3: slope change; I: indicator.
mathematical_explanation: Estimates immediate and gradual outcome changes at a specified interruption.
scope_note: Confounding concurrent events, secular trends, autocorrelation and seasonality must be addressed.

symbol_definitions: e(x): propensity score; T: treatment indicator; Y: outcome; ATE_IPW: inverse-probability-weighted effect.
mathematical_explanation: A propensity score summarizes measured treatment-assignment predictors; inverse weighting targets a treatment contrast.
scope_note: This is one estimator, not all propensity-score methods; unmeasured confounding, positivity and score estimation matter.

symbol_definitions: F_m: ensemble after iteration m; h_m: fitted base learner; ν: learning rate; γ_m: step weight.
mathematical_explanation: Gradient boosting incrementally adds learners to improve a chosen loss function.
scope_note: The loss, base learner and regularization differ by implementation; validation is essential to control overfitting.

symbol_definitions: λ≥0: regularization strength; β_j: non-intercept coefficients.
mathematical_explanation: Ridge regression shrinks coefficients continuously toward zero to stabilize prediction.
scope_note: Predictors should generally be standardized for penalty comparability; intercept is normally not penalized.

symbol_definitions: λ≥0: tuning penalty; β_j: non-intercept coefficients.
mathematical_explanation: LASSO’s absolute-value penalty can shrink some coefficients exactly to zero.
scope_note: Variable selection may be unstable with correlated predictors; inference after selection needs care.

symbol_definitions: λ≥0: penalty strength; α in [0,1]: mix between LASSO (1) and ridge (0).
mathematical_explanation: Elastic net combines L1 and L2 shrinkage to handle selection and correlated predictors.
scope_note: Exact penalty scaling differs between software implementations.

symbol_definitions: y_i in {−1,1}: class; φ: feature map; ξ_i≥0: margin violations; C: penalty.
mathematical_explanation: A soft-margin support vector classifier balances a wide margin against classification errors.
scope_note: This is classification SVM; support vector regression and other loss functions use different objectives.

symbol_definitions: N_k(x): indices of the k nearest observations; k: chosen neighbor count.
mathematical_explanation: For regression, kNN predicts the average outcome among nearby training points.
scope_note: Classification kNN uses voting; distance metric and feature scaling strongly affect results.

symbol_definitions: C: class; x_j: feature; P(C): prior class probability.
mathematical_explanation: Naive Bayes combines class priors with feature likelihoods to classify new cases.
scope_note: Assumes conditional independence of features given class, often only approximately true.

symbol_definitions: a^(ℓ): layer activation; W: weights; b: biases; σ: activation function.
mathematical_explanation: A neural network repeatedly transforms inputs through learned weighted nonlinear layers.
scope_note: This is a generic feed-forward layer, not a complete training algorithm or architecture.

symbol_definitions: C_k: cluster k; μ_k: cluster centroid; K: chosen number of clusters.
mathematical_explanation: K-means partitions observations to minimize within-cluster squared distances to centroids.
scope_note: Sensitive to scaling, starting positions and outliers; results need not reflect natural groupings.

symbol_definitions: A,B: clusters; d: observation distance.
mathematical_explanation: Agglomerative hierarchical clustering joins clusters based on a linkage-defined distance.
scope_note: Single linkage is one option; complete, average and Ward linkage use different rules.

symbol_definitions: ε: radius; minPts: required neighborhood count; d: distance metric.
mathematical_explanation: DBSCAN defines dense regions using core points and density-reachable neighbors.
scope_note: The neighborhood definition typically includes the point itself; ε and minPts affect clusters and noise labels.

symbol_definitions: h(x): path length to isolate point x; c(n): expected reference path length at sample size n.
mathematical_explanation: Isolation forest assigns higher anomaly scores to cases isolated by shorter random partition paths.
scope_note: Scores depend on forest construction and sampling; labels need a separately chosen threshold.

symbol_definitions: η_t: linear predictor; x_t-ℓ: historical exposure; B_j: exposure basis; C_k: lag basis; L: maximum lag; z_t: adjustment variables.
mathematical_explanation: DLNMs express a potentially nonlinear exposure–response association distributed over historical lags.
scope_note: This is a cross-basis term within a larger model; the response distribution, lag range, confounding, and temporal structure require separate specification.
